newsitem.title: USA: Missing Chinese girl found murdered in New York.
newsitem.headline: Missing Chinese girl found murdered in New York.

text.p: An 11-year-old Chinese girl who vanished in New York two weeks ago has been found strangled in Manhattan's East River, authorities said on Thursday.

Using dental x-rays, medical examiners confirmed their suspicions that the severely decomposed corpse retrieved from the river late Wednesday was that of Quin-Rong Wu, who came to the United States last year.
A spokeswoman for the medical examiner said the cause of death was manual strangulation. "It's a homicide," she said.
Police in a helicopter spotted the body floating near the Manhattan Bridge, authorities said.
Wu, who knew only a little English, was reported missing on May 13 after she failed to return home, police said. That morning, her mother had walked her to within one block of her Chinatown school.
On Tuesday, police released a sketch of a man who they said they were seeking in connection with the girl's disappearance.

A woman reported last weekend that she saw a girl fitting her description with the profiled man in the subway, an hour after she said goodbye to her mother. She was crying and looking lost, the woman said.
